'''''Rumex arifolius''''', common name '''maiden sorrel''' <ref name=future>[http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Rumex+arifolius Plants for a future]</ref> or '''mountain dock''',<ref name=luirig>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=rumex+arifolius+subsp.+amplexicaulis Luirig.altervista]</ref> is a leafy [[perennial]] [[herb]] in the family [[Polygonaceae]].

==Description==
''Rumex arifolius'' can reach a height of {{convert|70|-|120|cm}}.<ref name=future/> This plant has fleshy large leaves with entire blade margins. The inconspicuous white flowers and seeds are carried on long clusters at the top of a stalk arising from the axil of leaves. The flowers are [[dioecious]] and [[anemophilous]].<ref name=future/> They bloom from May to June.<ref name=luirig/>

==Taxonomy==
''Rumex arifolius'' was first described by [[Carl Christian Gmelin]] in 1806.<ref name=POWO_697191-1/>

==Distribution==
Maiden sorrel is native to southern Europe,<ref name=POWO_697191-1/><ref name=future/> and parts of northern temperate Asia.<ref name=POWO_697191-1/>

==Habitat==
This species prefers pine forests and mountainous meadows <ref name=future/> at elevation of {{convert|200|-|700|m}} above sea level.<ref name=luirig/>
